b. protect women and provide services to women and children victims of violence; and

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Batu Bara Regency.

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and DPRD according to the principle of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

6. Child protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.

8. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against Women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in suffering or distress to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

11. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.

12. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences l suffering and/ or distress as a result of

Violence and/ s or threat of Violence.

13. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.

14. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and normally both in the family and in society.

15.Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.

16. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence from the Region to their Region of origin.

17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND

CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 16

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:

a. establish family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

Article 15

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service implementation for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS Article 9

SPM for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence, includes services:

a. handling of complaints/reports of violence victims against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; and
e. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

S'

Article 14

Funding for the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, shall be sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
I

Article 12

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 17

In the event that PPT as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1) has not been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the duties and functions of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

Article 13

(1) The Regent is responsible for making reports on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

NUMBER 2 OF 2016

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND

CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children;

b. protect women and provide services to women and children victims of violence; and

c. empower women and children victims of violence.

Article 11

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the development and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

Article 16

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:

a. establish family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS Article 9

SPM for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence, includes services:

a. handling of complaints/reports of violence victims against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; and
e. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

Article 15

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service implementation for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND

CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The State has the obligation to provide protection to every c citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. that women and children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a human rights issue and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life or body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in public land or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

This regional regulation governs protection efforts for women and children victims of violence particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, financing, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence as well as to prevent and reduce acts of violence against women and children. r

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 16

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, the community may:

a. establish family partners at the Village/Sub-district level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children independently;
c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 13

(1) The Regent is responsible for making reports on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region to the Governor with copies submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES i

Article 15

(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service implementation for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CHAPTER XIII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

CHAPTER VI

MINIMUM SERVICE STANDARDS Article 9

SPM for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence, includes services:

a. handling of complaints/reports of violence victims against women and children;
b. health services for women and children victims of violence;
c. Social rehabilitation for women and children victims of violence; d. law enforcement and legal aid for women and children victims of violence; and
e. repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

Article 11

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the development and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in the Region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Work Units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence for the current year.

Article 12

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
